evidence.field: File summary, source attribution and license
evidence.text: The exact file page explicitly identifies 听-seal.svg as depicting 听 in Shuowen seal-script style. It points to Xiaoxuetang image 27.542C as the source and states CC0 1.0/public-domain terms. The file is a modern digital redraw, not an artifact photograph.
evidence.title: File:听-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.text: The inspected Original file link resolves to https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/ad/%E5%90%AC-seal.svg. The web tool's direct fetch returned a cache miss; this is an access limitation, not evidence that the file is unavailable.
evidence.title: File:听-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.field: Character form record; source label and image
evidence.text: The character-specific record for 听 labels the supplied small-seal form “小篆” and “說文‧口部,” then shows the corresponding regular-form label 听. Its linked image URL is https://xiaoxue.iis.sinica.edu.tw/ImageText2/ShowImage.ashx?color=%23000000&font=%E5%8C%97%E5%B8%AB%E5%A4%A7%E8%AA%AA%E6%96%87%E5%B0%8F%E篆&resolution=96&size=48&style=regular&text=%E5%90听. The label connects this database-rendered form to the Shuowen 口 section; it does not establish that it is an excavated artifact or show pixel-level comparison with the Commons redraw.
evidence.title: 小學堂字形

evidence.text: The official notice states that glyph images and glyph-attribute information obtained through the site's query interface are released under CC0 1.0, within the limits of law. This permission is scoped to those query-interface assets and information.
evidence.title: 版權聲明

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, online Shuowen Jiezi text with Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.field: 听 entry; definition, received component analysis and cited example
evidence.text: The page transmits 听 as “smiling appearance,” analyzed as 口 with 斤 phonetic, and gives 宜引切. Duan Yucai's commentary quotes Sima Xiangru's “亡是公听然而笑.” This supports describing the image as a Shuowen-section form associated with the old 听 entry; the text is the received lexicographic analysis, not independent proof of the graph's original formation.
evidence.title: 說文解字「听」

evidence.field: File summary, identity distinction, source and rights
evidence.text: The separate file 聽-seal.svg explicitly depicts 聽 in Shuowen seal-script style and gives CC0 1.0/public-domain terms. This is a different file and character from 听-seal.svg; the checked 听 attachment should not be described as 聽.
evidence.title: File:聽-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A03282-011 听 (聽); cited vernacular use and simplification
evidence.text: The 聽 entry lists 听 as a variant, cites 宋元以來俗字譜 for vernacular writing, and reports the standardized correspondence “聽作听.” This establishes a historically separate use of the same graph for 聽 by the Song–Yuan citation and its standardized simplified counterpart relation; it does not show that the old smiling-word use developed into hearing or that the depicted Shuowen form was used for 聽.
evidence.title: [A03282-011] 听 (聽) - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

search_audit.query: site:commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File 听 说文 小篆 听-seal.svg glyph identity 斤 口
search_audit.outcome: Search results located the exact 听, 聽 and 斤 Commons file pages. Opened all three relevant file descriptions; the 听 page explicitly labels the character and license, while 聽 is a separate file.

search_audit.query: Shuowen 听 seal script image 说文 听 笑皃 从口斤聲 小篆 image
search_audit.outcome: Opened the Commons 听 file record and Shuowen.org entry. The exact Commons Original file and Xiaoxuetang source-image links were followed, but both image fetches returned cache misses. The dictionary record confirms the received smiling gloss and 口 plus 斤 phonetic account.

search_audit.query: site:dict.variants.moe.edu.tw 听 聽 宋元俗字谱 standardized simplified 听 variant entry
search_audit.outcome: Opened the Ministry dictionary's 聽 variant record. It cites Song–Yuan vernacular sources and explicitly gives 聽作听 as the standardized correspondence.

gaps: The Commons description and the character-specific Xiaoxuetang record both identify a 听 small-seal form, but the web tool could not retrieve the direct SVG or linked raster image bytes (cache misses); no independent pixel-level comparison is claimed.

The image is a modern digital redraw / query-interface rendering in Shuowen small-seal style, not a photograph of an ancient artifact. Its association with the Shuowen 口-section record does not establish an archaeological date.
The attached file is explicitly identified as 听, while the distinct 聽-seal.svg file is explicitly 聽. Neither modern redraw alone establishes the historical path by which 听 later represented 聽.

items.period: Shuowen small-seal-script tradition; modern digital redraw
items.tradition: Small seal script, labeled 小篆 / 說文‧口部 by the character-specific Xiaoxuetang record
items.caption: A modern redraw of the small-seal form recorded for 听 in the Shuowen 口 section. The received Shuowen entry gives 听 the sense “smiling appearance” and analyzes it as 口 plus phonetic 斤; the image is not an artifact photograph.
items.alt: Black small-seal-style 听 glyph centered on a white square, with compact strokes at left and a broader curved component on the right.
items.selection_reason: The exact file record and linked character-specific database entry identify the glyph as 听 and associate the source form with the Shuowen 口 section. It is useful for illustrating the older 听 entry, while the later use for 聽 is separately attested and not implied by this image.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication; Commons also describes it as a public-domain picture of an ancient script. The linked Xiaoxuetang query-interface glyph imagery is separately covered by its CC0 notice.

limitations.text: The direct image and linked Xiaoxuetang image fetch returned cache misses, so pixel-level comparison was not performed here. The modern redraw is not an excavated artifact and does not by itself establish a date or a sequence of graphic changes. Song–Yuan vernacular evidence for 听 used for 聽 is separate from the old smiling-word record.
